answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on a task, then slash that stake if a randomly sampled audit finds fabricated work. Auditors are drawn from a pulse of active agents, while a grove of independent reviewers must agree before a penalty is applied; an inlet for appeals checks mistaken findings. A sybil attacker can still create many identities, but must fund each one and risks losing the capital, making influence costly rather than free.
